scope: Normative design closure for every catalogue operation; registration and qualification remain separate. Exact fields, numeric contracts and action spellings come from the catalogue and concrete headers. This file adds no guest export.

common.default_authority: Binding exposes two read-only queries by default: abi returns the public ABI major and permission.report describes the caller's own permissions. The host can deny or hide each independently. All other imports require explicit exposure, and resource operations also require the matching grant. Reading another module or the VM requires separate authority.
common.rate_progression: Call and byte limits govern admissions within an existing grant. An omitted rate allows unrestricted traffic within that scope. A zero window allowance refuses ordinary work with again (11) while the grant stays valid. A missing or revoked permission yields denied (13). A control phase with a rate limit needs an explicit missed-phase policy and independently reserved stop capacity.
common.origin_closure: Each supplied capability is checked on its own actual origin. Ancestors, inputs, control owner, active versions, egress and output destinations do not borrow the primary handle permission.
common.effect_classification: Classify the complete downstream graph, including ROS topics/services/actions/parameters, callbacks, bridges and native components. Unknown classification refuses effectful activation. Observation or planning never authorizes physical execution.
common.transaction: Validate input/output spans, finite decode/work budgets, selected semantic value schema, current authority and complete reply/recovery/retention before effects. No guest pointer survives the call.
common.concurrency: No authority/provider lock is held while waiting on IPC or invoking an external sink. Commit rechecks original identities/generations. Lock order and compound origin checks are provider obligations.
common.physical_execution: Require current ownership/mode, complete physical content validator, original trusted state/dependencies, receiver fencing, independent watchdog and stop reservations at actual effect. Native ACK is not independently observed safe state.
common.allocation: Owning admitted state uses recoverable project fast_io allocation. Null/failure returns before effect; ordinary terminating allocation is not an untrusted admission strategy. Borrowed codecs allocate nothing.
common.limits: Every variable record/list/queue/metadata/pin/process/thread/native workspace has explicit finite capacity. Fixed implementation ceilings are support limits, not portable semantic limits and not silent truncation.
common.lifecycle: Logical close/revoke does not reverse completed effects or free live borrows. Unknown physical/native outcomes retain identity and capacity through qualified reconciliation.
common.observability: Debug/IDE expose cached bounded redacted state/counters/reasons only. They cannot trigger I/O, grant authority, export paths/credentials/payloads, or rearm safety.
common.platform: Native extensions execute outside the VM in a qualified process boundary. Unsupported required isolation/placement/transport/cleanup guarantees refuse activation. No generic WASI or preloaddl fallback.
common.evidence: A schema, decoded record, registered import, native provider, VM qualification, differential ROS case, performance profile and physical assurance are distinct evidence levels.

discovery.commit: Return the explicitly exposed module major; do not discover hidden imports or provider features.
discovery.copy_failure: No output memory carrier and no state to consume.

capability_acquisition.commit: Resolve an exact existing alias and bind the actual caller incarnation. Publish a new handle without increasing its immutable grant ceiling.
capability_acquisition.retry: A repeat is a distinct handle acquisition; it does not reset grant counters or revoke existing handles.
capability_acquisition.retirement: Capability close does not retire borrowed resources or accounting.

capability_retirement.commit: Close an owned handle or execute the separately authorized revocation scope; fence further operations and wake affected work.
capability_retirement.copy_failure: Do not undo an already applied security restriction. Preserve bounded audit evidence.
capability_retirement.retry: Apply only the original owned scope; stale/closed identity cannot select a newer incarnation.
capability_retirement.retirement: Retained resources, pending effects and cleanup debt outlive logical revocation.

owned_creation.commit: Validate exact origin/profile closure; reserve the complete admitted object and dependencies before publishing its identity.
owned_creation.copy_failure: Rollback unpublished object and its own staged references; do not close parent/source objects.
owned_creation.retry: Without an explicit creation key a repeat is a new acquisition; it cannot implicitly renew a lease or reset state.
owned_creation.retirement: Release only after all retained borrowers, requests and native owners retire.

asynchronous_creation.commit: Record the owned monotonic creation key, deadline and origin closure before beginning bounded isolated native creation.
asynchronous_creation.copy_failure: Retain the same creation receipt; no duplicate native launch from a failed copy.
asynchronous_creation.retry: Exact key and content recover the same creation; changed content conflicts. communication.open.take publishes the endpoint.
asynchronous_creation.retirement: Undelivered/cancelled native owners remain charged until positive cleanup evidence.

owned_observation.commit: Authorize the complete visible origin and query; snapshot only the requested bounded result. Explicit timed queries may progress their documented provider state.
owned_observation.copy_failure: No queue acknowledgement, implicit resubmission or resource retirement from a failed copy.
owned_observation.retry: Repeat the query under current authority; snapshot cursors and generation must match their original filtered scope.
owned_observation.retirement: A read does not erase recovery or physical uncertainty; owned snapshot/page pins have finite lifetime.

local_mutation.commit: Validate all exact owner/dependency fields and complete mutation before committing within the owning registry.
local_mutation.copy_failure: Honor the concrete wire commit point; a failed post-commit copy is not automatic rollback. No external hardware effect is permitted.
local_mutation.retry: Use original offset/generation/sequence where provided. Unkeyed operations do not promise exactly-once replay.
local_mutation.retirement: Only owned local state changes; held references and sealed content retain accounting.

bounded_wait.commit: Reserve bounded output/wait capacity, release authority locks before waiting, then recheck current authority and the exact observed horizon.
bounded_wait.copy_failure: Do not consume readiness, messages or native acknowledgements on bad output.
bounded_wait.retry: A repeated wait observes current state; it never republishes a message or creates an acknowledgement.
bounded_wait.retirement: Cancel/shutdown wakes waiters; elapsed time never fabricates provider support.

consume_after_copy.commit: Reserve a whole owned item and its original metadata/correlation. Copy and revalidate before marking it delivered or advancing the queue.
consume_after_copy.copy_failure: Retain the same item or explicitly retire it only under revocation/deadline policy; failed copy cannot consume silently.
consume_after_copy.retry: Retry delivers the retained item while its original authority and lifetime remain valid. Duplicate successful consumes are not exact replay.
consume_after_copy.retirement: Pins and correlations survive logical handle close until their real borrower/recovery obligations finish.

owned_close.commit: Fence new work on the exact owned resource and apply its documented drain/cancel/safe-release policy.
owned_close.copy_failure: Preserve already-applied closure; close never resets budgets or reopens a source.
owned_close.retry: No handle reuse or closure of unrelated sources. Already-retired identities remain invalid under the concrete binding.
owned_close.retirement: Delay capacity release until borrows/native work/processes actually retire; physical unknown outcomes remain latched.

keyed_effect.commit: Decode the complete operation, validate original authority and secondary origins, and reserve reply/replay/effect capacity before recording the accepted request and crossing an effect boundary.
keyed_effect.copy_failure: Keep the same accepted receipt and any unknown effect; no automatic resend after failed delivery.
keyed_effect.retry: The exact original key and contents recover the retained receipt. Modified/out-of-order requests fail. Underlying native atomicity and cancellation are never inferred.
keyed_effect.retirement: Retain input pins, native correlation and cleanup/unknown debt through terminal evidence or qualified reconciliation.

owned_cancellation.commit: Fence only the owned pending request or local response interest; native cancellation exists only when the selected provider explicitly supports it.
owned_cancellation.copy_failure: Keep the observed cancellation receipt; do not convert lost output into another remote effect.
owned_cancellation.retry: Repeat observes the same owned request; abandoned service interest is not remote cancellation.
owned_cancellation.retirement: Already crossed effects remain represented and charged until qualified resolution.

callback_response.commit: Require the exact delivered owned callback, current generation and deadline, legal response and any independently granted transformed values.
callback_response.copy_failure: Preserve exact response recovery where the concrete provider defines it; never call guest code from a native callback.
callback_response.retry: Only the matching original response can replay; conflicting transformed content or callback incarnation is rejected.
callback_response.retirement: Resolving a logical callback neither rearms a device nor proves an external effect completed.

lifecycle_submission.commit: Commit only the next successful key, expected generation, legal transition, permitted mask and finite deadline; queue one guest callback.
lifecycle_submission.copy_failure: Retain the same five-word logical receipt.
lifecycle_submission.retry: Exact last successful submission recovers its receipt; rejected requests do not consume keys.
lifecycle_submission.retirement: Deadline enforcement of the local binding is on access; no autonomous physical watchdog is implied.

receive_reservation.commit: Reserve the exact complete owned delivery and expose its identity/metadata without acknowledging native consumption.
receive_reservation.copy_failure: Retain the original item/identity; do not leak a partial new reservation.
receive_reservation.retry: Only the same live reservation and owner can be acknowledged or released.
receive_reservation.retirement: Reservation capacity remains charged until acknowledgement/release or qualified provider retirement.

receive_acknowledgement.commit: Acknowledge only the exact current owned reservation after its checked delivery contract.
receive_acknowledgement.copy_failure: Do not acknowledge a different item or repeat a native effect because output failed.
receive_acknowledgement.retry: Idempotence is scoped to the concrete reservation identity; stale identities cannot consume a newer record.
receive_acknowledgement.retirement: Release only this reservation and its retained correlation according to provider rules.

receive_release.commit: Release the exact owned reservation without implying remote application completion.
receive_release.copy_failure: Do not alter unrelated queue entries.
receive_release.retry: Exact ownership and reservation incarnation remain mandatory.
receive_release.retirement: Return or retire only that item according to the explicit receive policy.

cache_transaction.commit: Use the per-alias successful next key and exact receipt reservation. Reserve the entire object; publish only complete immutable session content.
cache_transaction.copy_failure: Preserve the same nine-word receipt and allocated object; no duplicate append or mutation.
cache_transaction.retry: Exact last request replays; the next successful mutation acknowledges the prior receipt. Status/read calls do not acknowledge.
cache_transaction.retirement: Volatile publication is not durability. Borrowed published content and incomplete transactions remain charged until actual retirement.

recording_transaction.commit: Validate channel/source read and export authority; commit complete bounded records/checkpoints under the writer key and owned source pins.
recording_transaction.copy_failure: Retain exact receipt and checkpoint identity; no partial record publication.
recording_transaction.retry: Exact writer-key replay; record ordering and source generation remain unchanged.
recording_transaction.retirement: Current checkpoints are volatile MCAP objects; readers retain them independently of writer closure.

proposal_pipeline.commit: Capture authentic ordered inputs; authenticate a completed model result; independently admit the exact target action and its original origins at acceptance. Each stage requires its own grant.
proposal_pipeline.copy_failure: Keep its exact keyed record; no model output or failed copy may manufacture a target invocation.
proposal_pipeline.retry: Exact stage keys only; changed model bytes, target, input order/digest or source incarnation conflict.
proposal_pipeline.retirement: Capture/model/proposal pins remain accounted; acceptance never transfers or expands authority. Current target support is independently qualified.

bounded_logging.commit: Check the exact logger/severity/session sequence and explicit content budget; append inert private text without format-string execution.
bounded_logging.copy_failure: Keep the actual accepted/lost state, never claim durable audit storage.
bounded_logging.retry: Concrete session sequence controls duplicate handling; a loss counter cannot create execution authority.
bounded_logging.retirement: Bounded logging loss is observable and cannot consume independent stop/fault capacity.

terminal_release.commit: Retire only a terminal owned recoverable receipt whose native cleanup and borrowing obligations are complete.
terminal_release.copy_failure: Never forgive unknown effect or release a different request.
terminal_release.retry: A released identity cannot refer to future work.
terminal_release.retirement: Unresolved outcomes and cleanup debt block capacity retirement.

robot_provider.commit: Apply the operation-specific admission/effect/recovery rule in robot-provider-contracts.json; required native guarantees must be positively available before activation.
robot_provider.copy_failure: Apply that exact operation rule; never treat a decoded response as trusted physical evidence.
robot_provider.retry: Resource-scoped strict next key/exact replay for keyed mutations; inert opens roll back on delivery failure; unkeyed observations do not execute work.
robot_provider.retirement: Stop and unknown-effect reservations remain independent and survive logical closure.
